headline: Testing what biological foundation model embeddings encode across DNA, cells, and tissue
label: Biological Foundation Model Representations
summary: Four 2026 preprints apply uncertainty, equivariance, ground-truth benchmarks, and conditional generation to read or test foundation model representations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluating whether learned representations in biological models carry verifiable biological content, rather than treating embeddings and outputs as opaque. BASILISC attaches uncertainty to cross-modal single-cell correspondence and evaluates it against known pairings. The sparse autoencoder benchmark tests SAE features against known concepts across spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings, with consensus SAEs noted for reproducibility. RNA-SpecFlow reports that nucleus counts in its RNA-conditioned histology synthesis are sensitive to detector and pipeline choices, a readout-level caveat. HiFold-Mamba, a Stage 1 Registered Report, tests whether a reverse-complement-equivariant state-space model with an insulation-based loss improves DNA-to-contact-map prediction. What is new is the emphasis on uncertainty-aware, ground-truth-anchored assessment of representations. All four are preprints, so the evidence remains preliminary.
